prompt_text: Who is the best real estate agent in Pleasanton CA to sell my house?
answer_verbatim:
There’s no single objectively “best” agent for everyone — the right agent depends on your neighborhood, price range, timeline and priorities. I can, however, help you find the top agents in Pleasanton and give you a practical way to pick the best one for your home.

Quick plan you can use right now
1. Define priorities: do you want the highest net price, the fastest sale, lowest commission, or a stress-free full-service experience?  
2. Sources to find top agents:
   - Zillow/Redfin/Realtor.com agent rankings and past sales in Pleasanton zip codes (94566/94588).  
   - Local MLS (Bay East/BridgeMLS) sold data for similar homes.  
   - Google/Nextdoor community recommendations and Google Business reviews.  
   - Open houses in your neighborhood — see who’s active locally.  
   - Local real estate offices (Keller Williams Tri-Valley, Coldwell Banker, Compass, Berkshire Hathaway, etc.).  
3. Metrics to compare:
   - Recent sold volume in your neighborhood and price band (last 6–12 months).  
   - Average days on market and list-to-sale price ratio.  
   - Reviews and client references.  
   - Marketing plan (professional photos, video/drone, targeted buyer outreach, online ad spend).  
4. Interview questions to ask each candidate (keep it short; interview 3):
   - How many similar Pleasanton homes have you sold in the last 12 months? Can I see comps?  
   - What is your suggested listing price and how did you arrive at it?  
   - What’s your marketing plan and budget (photos, staging, online ads, broker tours, video)?  
   - What’s your commission and what services are included?  
   - Can you provide 2–3 recent local references?  
   - How will you communicate and how often?  
5. Red flags
   - Vague answers about pricing or marketing.  
   - No local track record or unwillingness to provide references.  
   - Promises to “guarantee” a price.  
6. Negotiation and terms
   - Compare net sheets from each agent (projected proceeds after all costs).  
   - Don’t choose solely on commission — weaker agents with lower fees can cost you in net price.  
   - Ask about short-term listing or escape clauses if you’re unhappy.

If you want, I can:
- Look up top-performing Pleasanton agents and give a short vetted shortlist (I’ll need your home address/ZIP and approximate price range or priorities).  
- Draft a short email or text you can send to agents when you request interviews.

Which would you prefer? If you share your address or target price, I’ll compile a personalized shortlist and suggested questions for each candidate.
